title: Reduce prompt-ingest CPU overhead via vectorized normalizer and LRU chunk-cache
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We observe ~25-40% of prefill CPU time consumed by prompt normalization and prefix handling on medium-length prompts (128-512 tokens). This is increasingly visible in low-latency SLO tails for hosted API customers. Goal: Reduce per-request ingest overhead by implementing a vectorized input normalizer (UTF-8 -> codepoint mapping, Unicode NFC normalization, whitespace collapse) implemented as a lightweight SIMD-capable microkernel, and add an LRU chunk-level cache for repeated prompt fragments (e.g., system messages, common instruction templates). This ticket focuses on the ingest-side pipeline (before tokenization handoff) and the local in-worker cache/eviction policy; later follow-ups will expose cache hints to the scheduler and to the routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end CPU time for prompt ingest stage reduced by >=30% p50 and >=20% p95 on benchmark suite (mix of short/medium/long prompts). 2) No change to tokenization correctness or Unicode normalization compared to golden corpus. 3) Added benchmark harness and CI job that fails if regressions >5% memory or CPU per-request. 4) Cache evictions/resizing metrics are visible in console dashboard and an SLO for cache hit rate >60% on synthetic workload.
implementation_plan: - Phase 1: Prototype vectorized normalizer in C++ with optional AVX2/NEON codepaths and a portable fallback. Integrate microkernel behind existing ingest abstraction. - Phase 2: Implement chunk-level LRU cache keyed by 64-bit content fingerprint (rolling xxHash64 of normalized bytes) with size accounting by bytes and entry expiration policy. - Phase 3: Wire metrics (hits/misses/evictions/avg-entry-size) and expose to Console (console-2026.03). - Phase 4: Run A/B using canary rollout on 10% of hosted inference traffic, monitor latency/CPU/correctness. - Phase 5: Roll out broader and document trade-offs and fallback knobs (disable SIMD, cap cache by memory).
design_decisions: - Use xxHash64 for cache keys to minimize compute vs collision risk; collisions handled by verification of normalized payload. - Prefer per-worker LRU over shared cross-worker cache to avoid synchronization overhead in hot paths. - Provide compile-time kernel selection with runtime feature detection: if CPU supports AVX2/AVX512/NEON, prefer vectorized kernel; otherwise fallback to scalar path. - Keep cache conservative by default (default 16MB per worker) to avoid OOM on small VMs. Users can tune via agent config.
benchmarks_and_results: Local microbenchmarks (AWS c6i.large equivalent) on mixed prompt suite (10k samples): baseline ingest CPU 11.3ms median, 48ms p95. Vectorized normalizer + 16MB LRU cache: 7.8ms median (-31%), 36ms p95 (-25%). Memory overhead per worker measured at +9MB (avg). Corner cases: massive single message (>=1MB) bypasses cache and uses streaming normalization to bound peak memory. Full cluster canary runs pending.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: SIMD kernels may mis-handle certain Unicode edge cases. Mitigation: add golden normalization tests and verification path that can optionally run on sampled requests. - Risk: LRU cache causes cache-thrashing with pathological workloads; mitigation: add adaptive admission (sampled LFU) and allow operator to cap cache to 0. - Risk: Increased GC/allocator pressure from caching; mitigation: use pooled arenas and evict large entries eagerly.
